articles.body: My second iPhone lives at home and I use it over a stream ( the setup ). The phone's own H.264 comes off USB at 20 to 50 Mbit/s, and the laptop's integrated GPU decodes and re-encodes it to a few Mbit/s so it survives a cellular link. The report was vague: sometimes the sound and the picture are out of sync. I had just fixed one audio-drift bug ( that story ), so I checked the audio path first. It was clean: no drops, no backlog. This time the picture was the late one. The number that looked fine The transcoder already logged its own added latency every five seconds: time from a frame arriving to its re-encoded version leaving. The median was 26 ms. Fine. The 95th percentile was 1 to 5 seconds. Not fine.

articles.title: SMS OTP Login Monitoring: GDPR Compliance and Phishing Risks Explained
articles.excerpt: Consider a hypothetical customer-support page: payment has settled, the receipt notification is queued, and the recipient cannot open the authenticated order page. The on-call sees a growing receipt b…
articles.body: Consider a hypothetical customer-support page: payment has settled, the receipt notification is queued, and the recipient cannot open the authenticated order page. The on-call sees a growing receipt backlog beside a successful SMS submission counter. A green OTP login counter would say little about GDPR compliance, either. Neither observation establishes that the right person can retrieve the receipt. For a pharmacy order, the same boundary matters when a refill alert leads someone back into an account containing sensitive information. Short answer: SMS OTP alone does not establish GDPR or PSD2 compliance, and NIST treats authentication over the public telephone network as restricted.

articles.body: Claude writes text and code. It does not render video. If you want it to hand you an MP4, it has to call a model somewhere, and the cleanest way to wire that up today is an MCP server. articles.body: Put three 3D models on a page and you get three separate worlds. Each <model> has its own space and its own lighting. If you want one block to sit on a board, you work out the numbers yourself or you write JavaScript to do it. In a post on the WebKit blog dated November 16, Brandel Zachernuk proposes giving that job to CSS. Safari on visionOS 27.3 includes a limited feature preview of the proposed spatial CSS API, starting with the <model> element. The post says spatial CSS "is made of a lot of small tweaks to existing syntax." That's what makes it interesting to me. The new parts look a lot like CSS you already write. To try it on Vision Pro or in the visionOS Simulator, turn on Settings > Apps > Safari > Advanced > Feature flags > CSS Portals.

articles.body: Watch a list of tickers for new SEC 8-K filings about executive changes (Item 5.02), material agreements and M&A (1.01, 2.01) and bankruptcy (1.03), and get only the filings you haven't seen yet, every day. Written with AI assistance and reviewed by the FedSignals Data team; we maintain these tools. When something big happens at a US public company, such as a CFO stepping down, a merger agreement being signed or a Chapter 11 filing, the company has to report it to the SEC on Form 8-K, usually within four business days. Each 8-K lists the events it reports as numbered items: 5.02 for officer and director changes, 1.01 for a material agreement, 2.01 for a completed acquisition or sale of assets, 1.03 for bankruptcy, and so on.

articles.title: Why Your Budgeting App Keeps Asking You to Reconnect Your Bank
articles.excerpt: If you use any budgeting app that connects to your bank, you have seen it. A banner says your connection needs attention, your balances stop updating, and a budget you trusted yesterday is suddenly wr…
articles.body: If you use any budgeting app that connects to your bank, you have seen it. A banner says your connection needs attention, your balances stop updating, and a budget you trusted yesterday is suddenly wrong. I build FinSight for a living, so I see this from the inside. Here is the plain version: it breaks for a handful of reasons, most are not your fault, and only some of them need anything from you. First, how the connection works Most budgeting apps do not talk to your bank directly. They use a connection provider, and for FinSight that provider is Plaid. You sign in to your bank through Plaid, your bank approves it, and the app gets permission to read your accounts. The app never sees your bank password. That middle layer is why things break in ways that look random.

Canadian Space Agency astronaut Joshua Kutryk was looking out one of the windows aboard the space station when the most incredible view came into focus — and thankfully he had a camera handy and was able to capture these striking scenes of the Himalayas from space. articles.title: Einstein was right! Scientists verify 1st image of a black hole ever captured
articles.excerpt: An independent team of researchers has validated the first image of a supermassive black hole captured by humanity, and that verifies Einstein's greatest theory.
articles.body: An independent team of researchers has validated the first image of a supermassive black hole captured by humanity. That, in turn, verifies Einstein's greatest theory, general relativity , which first predicted the existence of black holes and what their immediate surroundings would look like. Captured by a global network of telescopes forming an interferometer called the Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) and revealed to the public in 2019, the image shows the supermassive black hole at the heart of the galaxy Messier 87 (M87), located 55 million light-years away. The image of this black hole , designated M87*, with a mass around 6.5 billion times that of the sun, was an immense scientific achievement. That may lead to the question: why did it need verifying at all?
